title: Detroit Lions vs. Miami Dolphins Live Score & Stats – November 8, 2026 GameTracker Update (CBS Sports)
body:
The Detroit Lions rallied to a 31‑24 victory over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday night, turning a potentially demoralizing week into a showcase of resilience and depth. The win not only snapped Miami’s three‑game winning streak but also marked the Lions’ first triumph in South Florida since 2021, a feat that was amplified by the team’s ability to adapt after All‑Pro linebacker Jack Campbell suffered a severe neck injury during warm‑ups earlier in the week. Coach Dan Campbell’s “Play like No. 46” mantra—referring to the number on the Lions’ practice jersey that symbolizes perseverance—proved to be more than a slogan; it became the blueprint for a gritty performance that saw the Lions’ offense fire on all cylinders while the defense stepped up in the absence of their star linebacker.

From the opening drive, Detroit displayed a balanced attack that kept the Dolphins guessing. Quarterback Jared Goff, returning from a modest 2025 season, connected on a 45‑yard strike to wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown, setting up the first touchdown run by running back D’Andre Swift. The Lions’ offensive line, anchored by veteran left tackle Taylor Decker, gave Goff ample time to survey the field, a stark contrast to Miami’s earlier struggles against a stout defensive front. By halftime, Detroit led 21‑10, having capitalized on two turnovers forced by rookie safety J.J. Miller, who recorded his first career interception and a forced fumble.

Miami, playing without its starting quarterback due to a lingering ankle sprain, leaned heavily on rookie quarterback Tyler Huntley, who managed to spark a late‑second‑quarter rally with a 30‑yard touchdown pass to tight end Michael Mayer. However, the Dolphins’ offensive line faltered under the Lions’ relentless pass rush, allowing three sacks and a strip‑sack that set up Detroit’s second scoring drive. The Dolphins’ defense, meanwhile, could not contain Swift’s dual‑threat ability; the running back amassed 112 yards on the ground and added a 22‑yard reception that kept the chain moving and forced Miami into predictable third‑down situations.

The turning point arrived early in the fourth quarter. With the Lions clinging to a six‑point lead, Miami drove deep into Detroit territory, only to see Huntley’s pass intercepted by cornerback Jaylon Johnson, who returned it to the Dolphins’ 28‑yard line. The Lions seized the opportunity, and Goff orchestrated a methodical drive that culminated in a 12‑yard touchdown pass to rookie tight end Sam LaPorta, extending the margin to 31‑17. Miami answered with a quick strike to wide receiver Tyreek Hill, narrowing the gap to 31‑24, but the Lions’ defense held firm, forcing a three‑and‑out on the next series and sealing the win with a successful two‑point conversion.

Beyond the scoreboard, the game highlighted Detroit’s depth and coaching adaptability. In Campbell’s absence, inside linebacker Jarrad Davis assumed the leadership role, making 11 tackles and directing the defensive front with poise. The Lions’ special teams also contributed, as kicker Riley Patterson nailed a 48‑yard field goal in the third quarter, his longest of the season, and executed a flawless punt that pinned Miami inside its own 10‑yard line. For the Dolphins, the loss underscored lingering issues with pass protection and the need for a more consistent secondary, especially after a season‑ending injury to cornerback Xavien Howard that further thinned their defensive backfield.

Looking ahead, Detroit’s victory positions the Lions at 5‑4, keeping them within striking distance of a playoff berth in the tightly contested NFC North. The team’s ability to thrive without Campbell suggests a defensive scheme that can weather injuries, a promising sign as the regular season enters its final stretch. Meanwhile, Miami drops to 6‑3 and must regroup quickly; the Dolphins’ upcoming matchup against the New England Patriots will test whether Huntley can develop the consistency needed to sustain their early‑season surge. If the Lions maintain the confidence and adaptability displayed in Miami, they could emerge as a dark‑horse contender in the postseason, while the Dolphins will need to address their protection woes to avoid a late‑season slide.
